messages:
nina: Heads-up — onboarding run for `skua-embed-v1` completed on staging. Quick thread for failure modes we spotted.

omar: saw it, which tests failed?

nina: recall@1 dropped for very short queries (<= 6 chars) vs current prod (delta ~ -12%). Full recall@10 mostly fine.

kevin: interesting — any pattern in anchors or languages?

nina: concentrated on english short snippets and titles. clustering metrics: silhouette down 0.08 vs baseline. small clusters breaking into noisy centroids.

zoe: did we run per-length bucketing? can you paste the eval command?

nina: sure — run used: ```python eval/embeddings_eval.py --model skua-embed-v1 --dataset wiki-shorttail --buckets char_len:1-6,7-20,21- --k 1,5,10 --quant none```

kevin: thanks. also ran an int6 quantized trial earlier — results were worse than fp16 but not catastrophic. suspect quantization amplifies short-token signal loss.

maya: copied logs, here's the short-bucket breakdown we saw:
- baseline prod (heron-v2): recall@1 = 0.72, recall@10 = 0.91
- skua-embed-v1 fp16: recall@1 = 0.63, recall@10 = 0.88
- skua-embed-v1 int6: recall@1 = 0.51, recall@10 = 0.82

omar: that's a big hit at R@1. Any nearest-neighbor examples?

nina: pasted a couple:
```
query: "AI"
prod top1: "Artificial intelligence overview" (good)
skua top1: "AI research grants" (off, mismatch)

query: "NYC"
prod top1: "New York City guide"
skua top1: "NYC weather alerts" (kinda noisy)
```

zoe: looks like topological drift — small queries lose global context. Could be embedding normalization or tokenizer differences. Did tokenization change?

kevin: skua uses a slightly different token merge table we calibrated for perplexity earlier. That can change short-token embeddings a lot. Also check prefix KV caching — not relevant here but just noting.

maya: can we do a quick ablation: same model but force prod tokenizer and run the short-bucket eval? If it recovers, it's tokenization.

nina: running that now on a small sample. kick-off cmd: ```./ci/run_eval.sh --sample 10k --model skua-embed-v1 --tokenizer prod-tokenizer --buckets char_len:1-6``` (ci-bot will post when finished)

ci-bot: Triggered job 83421: skua-shortbucket-tokenizer-ablation (queued) :white_check_mark:

omar: also add a cosine-normalize step to the pipeline, just to see effect. we've seen norm changes help short queries before.

kevin: yes add `--l2norm true` to eval. if norm restores R@1 partially, then it's embedding scale shift.

nina: noted. if both tokenization+norm don't fix it, suspect training objective — maybe contrastive margin weighting downweights short seqs. I'll ask training to slice short examples and retrain small epoch.

zoe: also flag to infra: please don't roll this to canary until short-bucket looks within -3% R@1.

maya: creating a ticket for a canary hold and short-bucket alert.

nina: CI job finished — quick numbers: prod-tokenizer ablation bumped fp16 recall@1 to 0.69 (was 0.63). with `--l2norm true` -> 0.71. int6 still lagging: 0.55 with prod-tokenizer + norm.

omar: that's great signal — tokenization + normalization recovers most of the gap for fp16. int6 remains an issue; maybe calibrate per-channel quant scales or try per-tensor vs per-channel for weight quantization.

kevin: agree. next steps: (1) run per-channel int6 quant (2) ask training to add shortseq upweight in next tweak (3) hold canary until fp16+prod-tokenizer+norm passes threshold. I'll own quant experiments.

nina: assigning to @kevin and @maya for infra gating. I'll coordinate with training. thanks all. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: ticket ML-2487 created: "skua short-query recall degradation — tokenization/quant investigations"

zoe: good thread. let's reconvene after quant results.
